record.title: Random-current phase transition conjecture on the hexagonal lattice
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ be the hexagonal lattice. Denote by $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{H}}$ the single random-current measure and by $\phi_{\mathbb{H}}$ the associated random-cluster model.

$$

record.title: The characteristic-$p$ analytic cohomology conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a nonarchimedean field of characteristic $p$. Let $\Gamma$ be a compact $p$-adic Lie group, let $H$ be a pro-nilpotent closed subgroup of $\Gamma$, and let $M$ be a Banach space over $K$ equipped with a continuous analytic action of $\Gamma$.

**Characteristic-$p$ analytic cohomology conjecture.** (a) If there is a sequence of subgroups $H_j$ of $H$ forming a neighborhood basis of the identity such that

$$
H^i_{\operatorname{ct}}(H_j,M)=0
$$

for all $i\geq 0$ and all $j$, then

$$
H^i_{\operatorname{ct}}(\Gamma,M)=0
$$

for all $i\geq 0$. (b) If the action of $\Gamma$ is $K$-linear and there is such a sequence with

$$
\dim_K H^i_{\operatorname{ct}}(H_j,M)<\infty
$$

for all $i\geq 0$ and all $j$, then

$$
\dim_K H^i_{\operatorname{ct}}(\Gamma,M)<\infty
$$

for all $i\geq 0$.

This conjecture proposes extending the paper's main result from procyclic to pro-nilpotent subgroups. The pro-$p$ procyclic case is covered by the main theorem when the hypotheses hold for $H$ itself; the general pro-nilpotent case remains open.

record.title: Characterization of non-varying strata of quadratic differentials
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Q}_g(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ be a stratum of quadratic differentials, and let $L^+$ denote its value on the stratum. Assume that $\mathcal{Q}_g(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ is neither hyperelliptic nor irregular. Define

$$
S=\left\\{\frac{2k}{d_j+2}\mathrel{|}0<2k\leq d_j+1,\\ j=1,\ldots,n\right\\}.
$$

**Non-varying-stratum characterization.** The stratum $\mathcal{Q}_g(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ is non-varying if and only if $L^+$ equals the sum of the $g$ smallest numbers in $S$. record.title: Clifton–Huang conjecture on hyperplane covers of the hypercube
record.statement:

$$

record.title: Weaker distance-tree embedding conjecture for finite vector spaces
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\Delta\geq 2$. A **distance tree** is a tree whose edges are assigned nonzero distances in $\mathbb{F}_q^d$, and $\Delta(\mathcal{T})$ denotes its maximum degree. **Weaker distance-tree conjecture.** There is a constant $C_\Delta$ such that every $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^d$ with

$$
|S|\geq C_\Delta^{o(d\log q)}q^{(d+1)/2}
$$

contains every distance tree $\mathcal{T}$ with at most $|S|-100q^{(d+1)/2}$ vertices and

$$
\Delta(\mathcal{T})\leq\Delta.
$$

This weaker version replaces the conjectured error term $100q^{d+1}|S|^{-1}$ by the larger uniform error term $100q^{(d+1)/2}$, while retaining the near-spectral-size hypothesis on $S$.

Let $q=5^m$ with $m\geq3$ odd. Let $\mathcal C_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ be the BCH code appearing in the source, and let $\overline{\mathcal C}_4$ be the extended classical MDS cyclic code. **The minimum-distance conjecture.** Then

$$
d(\mathcal C_{(q,q+1,4,1)})=5
$$

and

$$
d((\overline{\mathcal C}_4)^\perp)=6.
$$

This is the remaining open case identified by the source for the minimum distance of $(\overline{\mathcal C}_4)^\perp$; it concerns the distance of a BCH code and its dual extended-code counterpart.

record.title: Ghosh et al.'s planar Turán bound for cycles
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $ex_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a planar graph on $n$ vertices that does not contain $H$ as a subgraph. Let $C_k$ be the cycle of length $k$.

**Ghosh et al.'s conjecture.** For each $k\geq 7$ and sufficiently large $n$,

$$
ex_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k)\leq 3n-6-\frac{3n+6}{k}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a general upper bound for the planar Turán number of every cycle of length at least seven, extending the known bounds for shorter cycles. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The exact failure criterion for the naive mod $\ell$ converse theorem for $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$
record.statement:

record.title: The strong parity property at the critical number of unoccupied vertices
record.statement:
Let $(d,k)$ be an admissible tuple of integers, and let $S(d,k)$ be the minimum integer such that $puz[d,k,S(d,k)]$ has the even solvability property. A configuration is $k$-mobile if it is not $k$-isolated or $k$-semi-isolated, and the puzzle graph has the **strong parity property** when it has exactly two components containing $k$-mobile configurations. **Strong parity conjecture.** The puzzle graph

$$
puz[d,k,S(d,k)]
$$

has the strong parity property. That is, it has exactly two components containing $k$-mobile configurations. record.title: Modular Erdős distinct subset sums conjecture

Let $t\geq 0$ be fixed and let $n$ be sufficiently large. Set $N=2^n+t$, and let $A$ be an $n$-element set of positive integers whose subset sums are all distinct modulo $N$. **Modular Erdős distinct subset sums conjecture.** One has

record.title: A weak polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture
record.statement:
Let $V$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-module, and let $A\subseteq V$ be a finite set satisfying

$$
|A+A|\leq K|A|
$$

for some $K\geq 1$.

**Weak polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that one can find $A_1\subseteq A$ with

$$
|A_1|>|A|/K^c
$$

and elements $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_d\in V$ for some $d<c\log 2K$ satisfying

$$
A_1\subseteq \mathbb{Z}\xi_1+\dots+\mathbb{Z}\xi_d.
$$

This is a weaker version of the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture, which seeks quantitatively optimal dependence on the doubling constant $K$ in Freiman's theorem. The surrounding discussion presents it as a central open problem in additive combinatorics with applications to the sum-product problem; no resolution of this weaker formulation is given here.

record.title: The bound-secrecy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be jointly distributed random variables, and let $S(X:Y||Z)$ denote the secret-key rate and $I(X:Y \downarrow Z)$ the intrinsic information. The **bound-secrecy conjecture.** There exists a distribution $P_{XYZ}$ such that

$$
I(X:Y \downarrow Z)>0 \quad\text{but}\quad S(X:Y||Z)=0.
$$

Such a distribution would exhibit secrecy between Alice and Bob that cannot be extracted as a secret key. The paper discusses bound secrecy as a significant open problem and notes that evidence for its existence would imply that the reduced-intrinsic-information equality conjecture is false.

record.title: Salehi-Golsefidy–Varjú super approximation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G<\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$ be a finitely generated subgroup. Let $\mathbb G$ be the Zariski closure of $G$, and let $\mathbb G_0$ denote its identity component. The group $G$ has the super approximation property with respect to all positive integers if and only if

$$
[\mathbb G_0,\mathbb G_0]=\mathbb G_0.
$$

**Salehi-Golsefidy–Varjú conjecture.** A finitely generated subgroup $G<\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$ has super approximation with respect to all positive integers exactly when the identity component of its Zariski closure is perfect. This gives a proposed characterization of super approximation for arbitrary finitely generated linear groups, extending the known results for important classes of Zariski-dense subgroups; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The concise symmetric Kronecker coefficient conjecture
record.statement:
For a partition $\lambda$, let $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ be the Kronecker coefficient and define the symmetric Kronecker coefficient by

$$
g_s(\lambda)=g(\lambda,\lambda,\lambda).
$$

A counting function is **concise** if every positive integer $k$ occurs as a value on an input whose size is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $\log k$. **Symmetric Kronecker coefficient conjecture.** The function $g_s$ is concise. The function is known to be complete and its maximum on partitions of size $n$ has exponential order, but the asserted polynomial-size realization of every value remains open.

record.title: Optimality conjecture for seven points spanning four distinct triangles
record.statement: A finite point set in the plane **spans four distinct triangles** when its triples of distinct points determine four congruence classes, up to rigid plane isometries. **Four-triangle optimality conjecture.** The maximum number of points in the plane spanning four distinct triangles is $7$, and equality is achieved only by the regular heptagon. This is a natural next case after the solved three-triangle case; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: The critical-snark Fulkerson-cover conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a critical snark, let a **hexagon** be a $6$-cycle, and let a hexagon be **double-core** when it is a double-core hexagon for a $3$-array of perfect matchings. An **optimal $3$-array** is a $3$-array leaving the minimum possible number of uncovered edges. **Critical-snark Fulkerson-cover conjecture.** Every hexagon in $G$ is double-core. In particular, every optimal $3$-array of perfect matchings extends to a Fulkerson cover. The claim is motivated by the fact that a double-core hexagon yields a Fulkerson cover; its general validity is left open.

record.title: Reciprocal supernorm max-part-statistic asymptotic conjecture
record.statement:
Let ${\rm Max}(n)$ be the ensemble of partitions with largest part $n$, and let $\widehat{W}_{\rm max}(n)$ denote its non-cumulative reciprocal supernorm statistic. **Max-part-ensemble conjecture.** One has

$$
\widehat{W}_{\rm max}(n) \sim \frac{e^{\gamma}}{n}
$$

as $n \to \infty$. This is the analogous prediction for individual max-part ensembles; the source gives no data because finite values require infinite summations, and no proof or resolution is stated.

record.title: Liu–Morris–Prince logarithmic-factor conjecture for multicolour connectivity
record.statement:
Let $f(n,r,s)$ be the smallest integer such that every $r$-edge-colouring of the complete graph $K_n$ contains a set of at least $f(n,r,s)$ vertices whose induced subgraph is connected using at most $s$ colours. Here $r$ is the number of colours, $s$ is the allowed number of colours, and $n$ is sufficiently large.

**Logarithmic-factor conjecture.** For any

$$
1\leq s\leq \frac{\sqrt r}{\log r}
$$

and $n$ large enough,

$$
f(n,r,s)=\frac{s^2(\log r)^{1-o_r(1)}}{r}\cdot n.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the logarithmic factor in the known lower bound is necessary throughout this range of $s$. It is motivated by the case $s\approx \log\log r$, where the authors show that a $(\log r)^{1-o_r(1)}$ factor is necessary; the general range stated above remains open.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Matija Bucić, Micha Christoph and Michael Krivelevich, “The power of many colours”, arXiv:2308.15387 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.15387

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: The Hochbaum–Nishizeki–Shmoys conjecture on polynomial-time edge coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let

$$
\Gamma(G):=\max_{H\subseteq G}\left\lceil\frac{|E(H)|}{\left\lfloor\frac{1}{2}|V(H)|\right\rfloor}\right\rceil
$$

be its density. A proper edge-coloring assigns colors to the edges so that adjacent edges receive different colors.

**Hochbaum–Nishizeki–Shmoys conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm that finds a proper edge-coloring of every multigraph $G$ using $\max\\{\Delta(G)+1,\Gamma(G)\\}$ colors.

The paper states that its main theorem confirms this conjecture by providing such an algorithm. Therefore the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Guangming Jing, “On Edge Coloring of Multigraphs”, arXiv:2308.15588 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Conjecture on maximum divergence from trapezoid models
record.statement: Let $\T_{a,b,d}$ be the trapezoid model in the simplex described above, with parameters $a$, $b$, and $d$, and let $D(\T_{a,b,d})$ denote its maximum divergence. **Trapezoid-model divergence conjecture.** The divergence from the trapezoid model $\T_{a,b,d}$ is at least $(a+b-1)\log 2$ and at most $(a+bd+b-1)\log 2$. This upper bound is sharp if and only if $d=0$. The preceding theorem gives a related upper bound, while the conjecture compares the trapezoid model with the two surrounding box models; the stated sharpness condition remains to be established.
